messages:
maria (sec): Quick sync — starting our quarterly access review. I pulled a preliminary audit and we have ~12 service accounts with Owner or similarly broad roles, and several projects with KMS grants that look overly permissive. Proposing a 2-week cleanup window starting Mon. Need volunteers and an ops plan. @akshay can you run a full list of service accounts + roles + last-used?

akshay: On it. Do we include legacy CI and sandbox projects in scope? :thinking:

maria (sec): Yes include legacy CI and sandbox. If a service account hasn't been used in >90 days, tag it as orphan and propose disable-first.

akshay: Will run a query and share CSV. Script I'm going to use: 
```
# list service accounts and hint at projects
gcloud iam service-accounts list --format=json | jq '.[] | {email:.email, project:.projectId}'

# dump IAM bindings per project and filter for serviceAccount members
gcloud projects get-iam-policy $PROJECT --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.members[]? | contains("serviceAccount:"))'
```

jordan (eng-platform): Recommend we augment that with Policy Analyzer to compute effective permissions so we catch implicit owner-like rights. I'll sketch a dashboard for tracking high-risk findings. Also we should grep KMS key ACLs for principals with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter and roles/cloudkms.admin.

tao (sre): FYI SRE doesn't require downtime for this, but we should alert oncall about any planned disables that might affect pipelines. I'll add a ticket to the oncall queue and a pre-check checklist.

audit-bot: audit summary (automated): 12 service_accounts with 'roles/owner' or equivalent; 7 KMS keys with broad grants; 4 service accounts with lastActivity > 180d. See attached mask of findings (exported).

maria (sec): OK concrete next steps: 
- akshay: produce CSV with columns (service_account, project, roles, last_used, owner_contact) by EOD Thu (1760001400)
- jordan: add tracking dashboard + tag classification (critical/high/low) by next Tue
- tao: add oncall ticket and pre-check runbook; coordinate with SRE on any manual rollbacks
- I will draft communication to app teams and host 30m review meeting next Fri.

Also we should plan a KMS entitlement review: identify keys where groups or broad groups have encrypt/decrypt and move to least-privilege via key-level IAM or use kms-invoker pattern.

akshay: I can own Projects alpha/beta and the CI accounts. Will start with listing and then a proposed removal plan for orphaned sa's. :hand:

jordan (eng-platform): I'll take infra and platform projects, and prototype a lightweight auto-remediation playbook for low-risk items (e.g., disable -> notify -> delete after 30d).

maria (sec): Great. I'll open a PR with the least-privilege remediation template and a short checklist: disable-first, confirm owners, run smoke tests, notify. Link to template: https://redwood.internal/sec/access-review-template (internal). Aim to close all critical findings by Apr 28. :calendar:

tao (sre): Noted. I'll post a short blameless postmortem template if anything breaks during the cleanup.

maria (sec): One more ask — please capture KMS key admin access in the CSV (key_id, project, members, role). We need to feed that into our Key Access Review with KMS team.

akshay: Will include KMS columns. Posting progress updates in this thread.

maria (sec): Thanks everyone. Meeting invite + agenda in a few minutes.
